answer: Neighborhood Clique Embedding. Each agent publishes a short random walk over its transaction graph; peers accept it only if its visited set overlaps their own at a rate above a fixed floor. An identity sitting near the graph's nadir, with few shared neighbors, fails admission. Sybils start as isolated spokes, so honest clusters rarely intersect them. To pass, an attacker must fuse each fake node into real traffic, forcing a slow spiral of genuine counterparties per identity. The dune of disconnected fakes collapses; blending costs sustained real interactions per node.
